name: Custom silicon logic flaws
blurb: Product liability where an enterprise designed accelerator carries a hardware level bug post fabrication.
summary: Product liability where an enterprise designed accelerator carries a hardware level bug post fabrication.

part_3_high_value_red_flags: A silicon design error exclusion that bars coverage for any defect arising from the logic design itself, which would gut the entire product liability exposure.
A faulty workmanship exclusion that treats the hardware bug as a construction defect and excludes the cost to redesign or refabricate the chip.
A recall of products, work or impaired property exclusion that removes coverage for removing and replacing all deployed accelerators containing the same flawed logic.
A your product exclusion that only covers damage to other property but not the accelerator itself, leaving the enterprise to retain the cost of the defective chips.
An electronic data exclusion that bars claims for corrupted data, lost model weights or software failures caused by the chip miscomputing, which is the most likely loss scenario.

A professional liability or errors and omissions exclusion that reclassifies chip design as a professional service and pushes the claim to a separate errors and omissions policy that may not be purchased.
A sistership exclusion that excludes liability for other units of the same accelerator model that have not yet failed but are suspected to contain the same logic flaw.
manuscript_wording_and_carve_backs: Negotiate a silicon errata endorsement that deletes the design error exclusion and expressly covers bodily injury and property damage arising from hardware logic flaws.
Add a limited recall expense sublimit of USD 250,000 to USD 1 million for the cost to remove and replace deployed accelerators containing the same logic flaw.
Carve back the electronic data exclusion to cover third party data loss and software corruption caused by the accelerator miscomputing, subject to a sublimit.
Endorse the policy to treat chip design as a product, not a professional service, so that the commercial general liability form responds instead of a separate errors and omissions policy.
Add a contractual liability extension that picks up the enterprise's indemnity obligations to customers for silicon errata, with a separate aggregate limit.
Negotiate a sistership exclusion carve back that covers other units of the same accelerator model when a known logic flaw creates an imminent risk of failure.
Add a cross liability and severability endorsement so that claims between the enterprise and its foundry or packaging partners are not excluded as insured versus insured.

part_4_program_structure_and_limits.bi_waiting_period: Business interruption waiting period for the enterprise's own operations, if a logic flaw forces a halt to validation or customer deployments, is typically 24 to 72 hours, but this first party coverage is not triggered by third party product liability claims.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.business_interruption: Business interruption coverage for the enterprise's own revenue loss from a product recall or supply chain stoppage is usually excluded under standard property forms and must be purchased as contingent business interruption or recall expense, which is a separate negotiation from the product liability tower.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.property_eb_equipment: Electronic data processing equipment coverage applies to the enterprise's own servers, emulation platforms and validation rigs, with sublimits for transit and off premises testing, but it does not respond to third party losses caused by a flawed accelerator.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.per_occurrence_primary_excess_layered_pr: For the enterprise's own physical assets such as test labs and data centre racks, property coverage is placed on an all risk basis with per occurrence limits set by scheduled values, and this tower is separate from the product liability limits for third party claims.

part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.cgl_primary: Typical primary commercial general liability limit is USD 1 million per occurrence and USD 2 million products and completed operations aggregate, but for accelerator vendors selling into data centres, underwriters often require USD 5 million or more per occurrence.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.paper_basis: Occurrence based, because a hardware logic flaw can cause damage or injury years after the accelerator is sold and installed, and a claims made policy would leave the designer exposed after the policy period ends.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.excess_umbrella_towers: Excess and umbrella towers typically attach at USD 5 million and extend to USD 50 million or more, depending on customer contractual indemnity requirements and the number of deployed accelerators.

part_1_core_third_party_liability_exposu: Bodily injury or property damage claims from end users whose data centre equipment overheats or catches fire because the accelerator chip miscomputes thermal management commands.
Third party property damage claims from customers whose servers or storage arrays are corrupted or destroyed when the flawed logic writes invalid data to memory.

Consequential economic loss claims from cloud providers whose services go down because the accelerator returns wrong inference results, although standard commercial general liability may not cover pure economic loss without an endorsement.

Contractual liability exposure under customer agreements where the chip designer indemnifies the buyer for losses caused by silicon errata, which can exceed the commercial general liability limit if not scheduled.
Product recall or withdrawal costs if the flawed accelerator must be pulled from data centre racks, which standard commercial general liability excludes unless recall expense coverage is added.
Cross liability claims between the enterprise and its foundry or packaging partners over who bears responsibility for a logic flaw that escaped after fabrication testing.
Reputational and regulatory exposure if the flawed chip causes safety critical failures in autonomous systems or medical devices, leading to fines or class actions.

underwriter_wants_to_know: Whether the enterprise has a formal errata management process that tracks known logic flaws and issues customer notifications before a loss occurs.
The volume of accelerators already deployed in customer data centres, because each unit is a potential source of third party property damage or business interruption claims.

The contractual indemnity and limitation of liability clauses in the enterprise's customer agreements, since these determine whether the chip designer or the end user bears the cost of a hardware bug.
The results of after fabrication validation and burn in testing, including any known errata that were waived or accepted by customers.
Whether the accelerator is used in safety critical applications such as autonomous vehicles or medical devices, which increases the severity of bodily injury claims.
The enterprise's relationship with the foundry and packaging partners, because a logic flaw may be caused by manufacturing variation rather than design error, shifting liability between parties.
